claims.object_text: epilepsy of infancy with migrating focal seizures
claims.quote: The most characteristic syndrome related to KCNT1 is epilepsy of infancy with migrating focal seizures.

claims.object_text: sleep-related hypermotor epilepsy (SHE) of frontal origin
claims.quote: Unifocal epilepsies have also been reported, the most common being sleep-related hypermotor epilepsy (SHE) of frontal origin.

claims.object_text: focal extrafrontal epilepsies with an insulo-opercular or temporal origin
claims.quote: Only 10 cases of focal extrafrontal epilepsies with an insulo-opercular or temporal origin have been reported.
Among these patients suffering from focal epilepsy, only seven underwent stereoelectroencephalography (S-EEG) describing focal or multifocal ictal onsets.

claims.object_text: refractory magnetic resonance imagining-negative SHE with insulo-opercular seizures
claims.quote: two unrelated patients suffering from refractory magnetic resonance imagining-negative SHE with insulo-opercular seizures.

claims.object_text: multifocal, bilateral, and migrating ictal activity
claims.quote: The four S-EEGs revealed multifocal, bilateral, and migrating ictal activity, whereas clinical ictal semiology remained stereotyped.
a pathogenic missense variant of KCNT1 was found in each patient (p.Arg928Cys and p.Arg933His).

claims.object_text: IO-SHE represents the second most frequent type of KCNT1-related focal epilepsy
claims.quote: IO-SHE represents the second most frequent type of KCNT1-related focal epilepsy

claims.object_text: migrating ictal activity might be a common feature of KCNT1-related epilepsy despite different syndromic presentations
